definition: A Multi-AZ DB instance keeps a synchronous standby for automatic failover that serves no reads. Read replicas replicate asynchronously to scale reads. Remember: Multi-AZ for availability, replicas for reads.
Daily snapshots plus transaction logs, kept 1 to 35 days, enabling point-in-time restore into a new instance. Manual snapshots last until you delete them.

Fully managed connection pooler for RDS and Aurora. Cuts failover time, enforces IAM authentication, uses Secrets Manager credentials, never public. Remember: Lambda functions exhausting database connections.
Managed RDS for Oracle and SQL Server that also lets you access the underlying OS and database for custom patches and settings. Remember: RDS plus OS access.
Six copies of data across three Availability Zones, storage that grows automatically, up to 15 low-lag read replicas, and automatic failover to a replica, typically in under 30 seconds.
The writer endpoint always points to the primary. The reader endpoint load balances connections across replicas. Custom endpoints target a chosen subset, such as larger replicas for analytics.

One primary Region plus read-only secondary Regions, replicated with typically under one second of lag. Promote a secondary in under a minute. Remember: cross-Region disaster recovery and low-latency global reads.
Aurora capacity that scales automatically in fine-grained steps and can pause at zero when idle. Remember: unpredictable, intermittent, or new workloads with no capacity planning.
Backtrack rewinds an Aurora MySQL cluster in place to an earlier time without a restore. Cloning makes a fast copy-on-write copy, ideal for a staging database from production.

Redis OSS or Valkey: replication, Multi-AZ failover, persistence, backups, sorted sets for leaderboards. Node-based Memcached: multi-threaded, sharded, no replication or persistence. Remember: Redis for availability.
Lazy loading fills the cache only on a miss, risking stale data. Write-through updates the cache on every database write, keeping it fresh. TTLs expire old entries.
Relational: RDS or Aurora. Key-value at any scale: DynamoDB. MongoDB: DocumentDB. Graph: Neptune. Cassandra: Keyspaces. Time series: Timestream. Analytics warehouse: Redshift.
Managed time-series database for IoT and operational metrics. New customers now use Timestream for InfluxDB, since Timestream for LiveAnalytics closed to new customers in 2025.
Serverless SQL queries directly on data in S3, priced per terabyte scanned. Cut cost with Parquet or ORC, compression, and partitions. Federated queries reach other sources through Lambda connectors.
Columnar, massively parallel data warehouse for OLAP and BI, provisioned or serverless. Redshift Spectrum queries S3 data without loading it. Remember: complex analytics and joins, not OLTP.
Managed search and analytics engine for full-text and partial-match search on any field, plus log analytics and dashboards. Often paired with DynamoDB to add search. Provisioned or serverless.
Managed Hadoop and Spark clusters on EC2 for big data processing. Keep primary and core nodes stable; task nodes are ideal for Spot. EMR Serverless also exists.
Serverless BI dashboards powered by the SPICE in-memory engine, with row-level and column-level security. Now named Quick Sight, part of Amazon Quick.
Serverless ETL, such as converting CSV to Parquet. The Glue Data Catalog holds table metadata for Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR; crawlers fill it. Job bookmarks skip processed data.
Builds a secure S3 data lake in days on top of Glue, with central fine-grained permissions, including row-level and column-level filters, enforced across Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR.
Serverless real-time stream processing with Apache Flink, formerly Kinesis Data Analytics. Reads from Kinesis Data Streams or Amazon MSK, not directly from Firehose.
Fully managed Apache Kafka, provisioned or serverless, running in your VPC across multiple Availability Zones. Remember: existing Kafka workloads move to MSK without code changes, unlike Kinesis.
